item.title: Contra Eneasz on shrivelling your balls
item.dc:creator: Frerk
item.description: I’m so tired. So jetlagged. It’s been hitting me hard. What can I do… I can’t even like… let’s see. Maybe I’ll crank up my macbook pro to 1000 nits. Ahh that’s better. So bright. Maybe increase the…
item.content:encoded:
CW: ageing, tiredness, jet-lag, mid-life.

I’m so tired. So jetlagged. It’s been hitting me hard. What can I do… I can’t even like… let’s see. Maybe I’ll crank up my macbook pro to 1000 nits. Ahh that’s better. So bright. Maybe increase the size of the text. 200%. Yeah that’s better. Still not very sharp. I think I need reading glasses. I had bought some a few months ago, but figured I don’t really need them. You know why people start needing reading glasses around 40 right? It’s because the eyes have focused too many times and the eyes can only focus so many times in your life and then they just wear out and go baggy like an old car something. I don’t have any metaphors. Maybe I don’t need any metaphors. It’s upsetting enough as it is. I asked claude code for an upsetting metaphor and he snooped through all my shit and somewhat freaked me out. AI definitely will kill us. Maybe my contact lenses are just a bit wonky from my nap, which didn’t help at all. I’m so out to lunch. It’s interesting that jetlag gets worse as the sleep debt accumulates. I’m having too much caffeine… Chugged cold brew (200mg of caffeine) after the nap on top of that celsius and a coffee this morning. The yanks are crazy with their energy drinks. If their pro-lifers were really serious they’d start protesting outside of the celsius plant, that stuff is pretty much plan b. I thought it’s good to have a bit more caffeine when you’re jetlagged. Tell the ol’ body it’s daytime. Nope.

Okay, whatever, let’s check the slack, see what’s new. Eneasz has a new post out on ageing. That’s my jam. Let’s see. He recommends I should have my t-levels checked, take finasteride, and freeze my spunk (his words not mine). Yeah, some TRT would be great right now. I’d kill for some TRT right now. But then it shrivels your balls no? I don’t want them to shrivel. I don’t want to take another thing.

I hate to brag but my t used to be high actually. They checked it when I was like 20 and they told me it’s at almost dangerous levels (my doctor’s words not mine). Ironically, t raises your estrogen as well and gave me unilateral gynecomastia aka one small booby. It’s only like an A cup. My mum told me it was because I drank too much beer as a teenager and I shouldn’t drink so much beer. No it was because I was high t, mum. Dangerously high t as it turned out, in fact. Now, it’s at a more moderate, reasonable, dare I say average level. Maybe that’s why I’ve mellowed. I had it tested a few years ago, actually, because they target you online, big TRT, they really hunt you down with targeted ads online, they really do. “Are you sometimes tired?” Why yes. “Are you feeling sad sometimes?” How did you know? “Would you like to have more energy?” They know you well and they start targeting you the first time you google ‘fleabag s01e01 torrent’.

I mean it would be nice to drink with both hands from the wellspring of youth and just chug that trt, quenching your youth thirst and feel that energy, that old ancient primal energy, that youthful male, yang, that source of all desire, flow through you, just once more, and illuminate everything around you like when Bradley Cooper does the adderall in Limitless, oh that t, only men know what it’s like, sorry ladies who aren’t on t, going out with your band of brothers on a stag hunt, you like your brothers, you like them strong, your brothers in arms, feel the blood of your enemies running through your fingers, later you huddle together around the fire with your strong brothers, you’d die for them, that’s how much you like them, you’re roasting the meat, you share the meat with your t brothers, and they share it with you, they really have your back, you groom each other reciprocally , you eat their lice to decrease their parasitic load, it’s a win-win, you’re the t brothers, all muscular and chissled, you’re all doing paleo, no need for glp-1s, the abs showing through your elegant pelts, you and your t brothers, strong and united, you play five-a-side and win the lower league with your young and strong t brothers and go to the pub after to drink the beer, sure, there’s some phytoestrogen in it maybe, your elders have warned you about it, but it tastes so good after a game with your t brothers, nothing like straight male friendship, nothing is quite like it is my point, sorry ladies, everything else is fake. God, I wish I was less male lonely.

Re: Finasteride…  I mean that ship has so sailed for me. I did look into it when things started. I remember when I first started balding. Oh boy, that one I do really remember distinctly. 23-years-old in an elevator with mirrors all around me. Long flowing hair I had then, and my whole life ahead of me. There it was. A clear bald patch. ‘ello pecia. That’s when it went all downhill. I talked to my american college ex gf on the phone about, upset, she laughed and said it had already started earlier. Women can be so cruel sometimes. Ironically, I think it was because of the high t. At least I got my beard. You win some, you lose some.

The spunk freezing. Yes, yes of course. Yes, of course, I’ve looked into it. The poor man’s cryogenics. Everyone’s been telling me. Like a few months ago, a colleague told me at the office. She had a STEM background and said she had read all about it and men also need to freeze. Men need to do it too she said, contrary to popular perception. You gotta. But I don’t know. I’m not saying don’t do it, I’m really tired and am not thinking clearly, but like, I do remember looking into it and thinking is it really worth it? I had it on my to do list for a while, but like you can’t do everything, no? It’s like guys, we've got literally hundreds of millions of gametes per pop and only the best one wins. That’s why we’re all so pretty. That’s why there have been many old fathers. Like aren’t there a lot of children of fathers who are like 70? Isn’t the base rate for a bunch of congenital stuff you can’t screen for is quite low anyway? I guess when I was younger I imagined that the whole procreation thing would be more carefree and all fun and creampies and now it’s all so clinical with the jizzing in cups and interviews on the Hinge meat market about how much you earn and Chris Olah’s achieving desired family size table with and without IVF and feeling ambivalent about dating women who are increasingly younger than you. Yes you heard me, I get older but they stay the same age, which is 34. I guess that’s fine for now, women love a zaddy, I hear. It’s bad though the messaging to younger men. They always tell you ‘you’ve got time for kids’. I think that’s bad. That’s literally what they tell you: ‘You’ve got time… focus on your career. You can find a woman of child bearing age when you’re 50.’ (their words not mine). They don’t want you to have kids, they want you to be a better short-term consumer. So yeah I think my advice for young men is: knock ‘em up while you’re still young maybe. Within reason obviously, jesus, will you relax. Women prefer men to be 3-6 years older on average and 23 cm taller. The important thing is to not overthink things like such statistics though and rather listen to your heart and start acting. Read less. Let go and stop toying with the imaginings of the unattainable. Meditate less. Start acting.

I don’t know… maybe kids are too stressful anyway. Bryan Caplan says you should have more kids but he says so much shit. Like he was so wrong on everything. He’s literally an imbecile. You realize he believes in contracausal free will right? He believes that poor people are to blame for their poverty because they didn’t get a high school degree BUT ALSO education is just signaling. He believes in open borders and we all know how that turned out. He says ADHD is just a preference for novelty and a strong disutility for work. Fuck you caplan, I’m not taking any family planning advice from you. I was talking to a young man about this morning. About having children. It’s hard to say what to do really, seems quite a different life. Kids won’t let you sleep I hear, they are not unlike this terrible jet lag. Maybe if I had a local community with brothers to protect each other’s children. Maybe if I had more energy. Maybe I’ll look into trt again. ba dum tsssssss 🥁.

Frerk, is a 40-year-old independent research artist living with his vacuum robot in a small studio (but pretty central). He is a-okay, don’t worry about this unhinged post, I’m just kiddin’, I’m still so jetlagged.

item.title: Ratfucker AI
item.dc:creator: Frerk
item.description: We’ll probably soon see much more AI-enabled ratfucking (automated opposition research on mostly true material), powered by decision models and LLMs, and I predict a decent chance of a…
item.content:encoded:
We’ll probably soon see much more AI-enabled ratfucking (automated opposition research on mostly true material), powered by decision models and LLMs, and I predict a decent chance of a Ratfuckopocalypse next year that might dominate the media cycle and have national security implications. Like, think about it, for example soon every intern with too much access can say something like:  

“@Claude: Go through the entire slack/intranet and tell me what the worst thing people have done at this company in the past.”

The AIs will dig up a lot of kompromat.

It’s starting already, cf someone used AI to collect the ‘most damning quotes’ and mapped the funding of EAs – in their own words.

Decision models like Jev are up to ~2 OOMs cheaper than frontier LLMs, and so far ~nobody has spelled out what that means: you can run a yes/no “is this damning?” filter over millions of messages, emails and documents for a few dollars, then hand the hits to a stronger LLM to connect the dots.

Some of the scandals might be justified, others might not. Small world networks and few degrees of separation between any one mean that anyone can be accused of being guilty by virtue of association. Like, did you know Dario Amodei’s wife once started a porn company and pitched it to Jeffrey Epstein, the pedo, for investment? I read it in the WSJ recently. Most often there’s more to the stories than the headlines suggest, or like in this case it’s a nothingburger, but few people read past the headlines, and headlines might be enough to stir things up and create controversy.

This probably has nat sec implications, with state actors leaking or amplifying kompromat and this just became much less expensive. Remember how Germany’s minister for defence lost his job because he plagiarized in his doctoral thesis? There were about a dozen other high-profile cases like that at the minister level in Europe in recent years and that’s just with access to their publicly published theses using crowdsourced wikis.

The scandals might also flood the zone and polarize society and cause anomie:

Perhaps this might also influence elections and lead to more populism.

Perhaps there’ll be lots of ransomware coming too. It also intersects with weak cybersecurity.

Maybe the vibe will shift even further away from cancel culture and people will mellow a bit more and move towards  ‘judge not lest you be judged’ or they’ll realize that morality is surprisingly detailed. People might start to become more privacy focused and record less information. It’s unclear what can be done about this aside from speeding up this process. And I haven’t seen much discussion about this but it seems that it might potentially be a fairly big deal.

On the other hand, maybe this will be bottlenecked by attention, not dirt, and after a few massive drops people will get scandal fatigue.

It doesn’t seem like we need any further technical advances for that and, in contradistinction to say bio- or cybersecurity, AI companies might not be able to put in ‘safety filters’ here.  I think this might potentially be really big.

item.title: Reading too many posts causes premature cognitive decline
item.dc:creator: Frerk
item.description: I can’t quite remember exactly where and when I noticed it the first time, which is ironic, but it must have been when I was merely around 33 years old and I also I do remember the event itself very…
item.content:encoded:
I can’t quite remember exactly where and when I noticed it the first time, which is ironic, but it must have been when I was merely around 33 years old and I also I do remember the event itself very vividly: I was watching a documentary that was a little bit meh but everyone was talking about it and it had such a high RT score when around halfway through the film there was a BIG OL’ reveal: the documentarian uncovered a tickle torture porn ring! But it was not the tickle torture porn ring that took me by surprise, but that I had seen the exact same film before and forgotten the entire set-up and everything leading up to the big reveal.

How-oh-how could I have forgotten that tickle torture porn ring? How was that possible? Do I fashion myself an infovore and a man of culture? Yes. And yes, I have seen that Werner Herzog movie where the guy gets eaten by the bear. True, maybe I did watch too many movies then and it all became a bit of a blur but it wasn’t that that many. Do I love drinking? Well, also yes, but not so much that my axons were demyelinating. Was I just an old baldy then? Well, I was but I was hiding it well and I did get MSP. And I was only a third of a century old; why-oh-why was this shit already starting at this age?

My undergraduate major in social and cognitive psychology (a discipline now mostly discredited), too, is a bit hazy, but this was partly the concerta and partly because my English was still developing and there’s a strong relationship between language and memory. I do distinctly remember an experiment from undergraduate psychology about the causes of childhood amnesia being due to the lack of language development where they showed young kids like some really memorable event and they found that only the kids who had the words to verbalize it could recall it at a later stage. Would it replicate? ‘I want to believe’.

But the other thing I remember from that course on memory is that the reason for why we ‘forget’ things as we age. It’s not that we actually forget things, it’s that we mostly have trouble recalling.

When you’re very young, you only know one of white male actor, say Matt Daemon, because all you’ve watched is Good Will Hunting. But then you watch too many movies and you know so many white male actors, and when you try to retrieve it there’s a certain probability mass on each of them. What was his name again, that actor, what’s his face, the guy who played Bond after Pierce Brosnan? You’re pretty sure it’s not Michael Cera, but there it could be so many others that roughly fit the bill.

It’s unsettling, but you learn to live with it. You start masking ‘Oh yeah long time no see, how’s it going ehem…  oh, yeah, I remember you, but you have so many meetings at EAG.’  It’s not early-onset Alzheimer’s, but it’s not not early onset Alzheimer’s either, in that it’s progressive and spreads to other areas of life outside of film trivia. Like, true, you’ve always been a ladies man and you don’t have to brag, but it wasn’t that many (indeed far too few), yet never had you thought you’d forget any of them, but then you did (it’s good that you keep a list, again, not because there were so many, but due to my issue with the retrieval).

So what to do about it? Maybe it’s all just too much. Too much gunk, gunking up your brain. You need to unsubscribe. Unsubscribe from everything. Clear out the cache. Do a reboot, make room for new stuff, but be more selective. Maybe it’s time to settle down. No more Feeld (not that it’s ever been easy there), no more South Park. Get back on the horse, get back on Hinge, find a wife, and only watch the highbrow stuff, the stuff that’s edifying, only the major HBO shows. Only what Tyler Cowen recommends, nothing Scaruffi rates less than 7.2 or maybe 6.9. But even that’s too much isn’t it? And besides it’s too dry and heavy. There’s too much content that’s for sure. Maybe I could use spaced repetition to drill and solidify the facts about friends and loved ones and my godchildren and then I could play GTA VI when it comes out.

Maybe go to Inkhaven, read the greats. One of the organizers read thousands of essays, and he seems pretty stable still. But on some level that seems insane to me. Everyone’s writing so much… who has the time and wherewithal to read all of that?

I mean does anyone even subvocalize anymore? Are you really savouring the fiction you read? Or are we all merely skimming at this stage. Just getting through it. Come on Proust, just get to the god damn point already. What's the bottom line? BLUF! Apparently, Marcel becomes a novelist.

Do you ‘member when you were young and it was so joyous to read novels? Took your sweet time reading all those novels, didn’t ya? Subvocalized. Yeah, I ‘member. But do you remember when you first tried to get into speed reading in college? They gave you all these readings and then there were even optional readings but it's just too much. You spend hours in the library and you can't possibly get all the reading done. But maybe you're a completionist. You start doing the math: 'well I read 14 pages this hour, and the syllabus has x, and there are y courses so, how do I get through all the reading? How would anyone? Even your literature professor says ‘Even if you read 100 books a year, that’s just at most a few thousands during your life time.’ Your college girlfriend says the professor gives her the creeps. Not in a harrassy way but one time they had a meeting his glasses cracked for no apparent reason. He was kind of weird that guy. Why was he reading all these books for? I guess he was teaching literature. You start thinking: maybe I'm a slow reader... is there a way to speed that up? You look into speed reading. They tell you not to subvocalise. They tell you subvocalisation is the devil. They tell you subvocalization is for the actually imbecilic. But it's just kind of skimming. But like... aren't thoughts words? How would you not subvocalise? Apparently, ‘language is primarily a tool for communication rather than thought’, there was a Nature paper that I meant to read. But is that true for wordcels? Is speed-reading all bs like hypnosis? I remember they did test them on some tv show and gave some speed readers long books and asked them questions and they answered them correctly. But maybe they were just using some really high-level heuristics? There are probably no good papers on that. I call bs. Like sure you can skim. You get better at skimming with age too, especially w/ stuff that is highly structured like scientific papers. But the entropy in good literature should be sufficiently high that makes skimming somewhat pointless. It's like listening to podcasts and audiobooks. Some nonfiction I can listen to at 3x the speed because it's just so nonfiction drivel that doesn't cause much surprisal at all. But then literature... Why would you speed read that at all? Just to get the cliff notes? Why not read 'save the cat' and learn about the basics of narrative. I've never read 'save the cat' but I've always wanted to. Maybe if I had a more abstract theory of how narrative works I could be more like von Neumann? Or at least like Lena Dunham… she said Jenny Koenner told her everything about b-story lines and stuff. Meow.

A related thought I had about this recently (suave segway): what's the deal w/ all these kids who are like in their early 20s having like this agenda to have the most sophisticated taste in art possible by just approaching it really systematically and just read what Tyler Cowen and Scaruffi recommend? That's kind of fucked up. I was talking to one of these kids once and it seems like they've listened to everything and seen all the important films, but like, it does seem a bit weird. Don't you have to watch some bad movies sometime or discover stuff through serendipity? Don’t you need live experience? One of them said their favourite FJM song is ‘Leaving LA’. As if. Isn’t art kinda subjective or something? Isn't the best music the music that you listen to during formative moments of your life, like when that older american woman living above you recommends the magnetic fields? God she was fiiiine. First time you saw her you couldn’t stop staring and things happened because you still had fantasies and could act on your desires. Now you’re on SSRIs and GLP-1s and you’re like bread on a stick. Even friggin’ TLP tells you to read the primary sources, but maybe: fuck that? Maybe I don’t want to be led by TLP anymore. Maybe that’s the lesson. I just need to get my fantasies and healthy desire back. It’s all noise. It’s all too much. What do all these dead white guys know anyway. Didn’t they believe that women had more teeth than men and we should set widows on fire and isn’t that suggestive evidence that are wrong in all the other important ways as well? And it’s all so heavy and dry. I say: don’t read the research digests either. Brevity comes from selection not compression.

Don’t read anything at all I guess is the lesson. There, I said it. Touch some grass maybe. Writing on the other hand. Oh yes, writing is thinking. The stuff of thought. Start creating, stop consuming. But then what should you write about? I need inspiration. I recently came across the wikipedia article on philosophical fiction. Tempting no? Maybe I am in the market for a new novel after all. Or maybe I should give Knausgaard another try, I guess he’s in my reference class, but then what does he know? Maybe more Rachel Cusk. Maybe read only women, but not performatively. Like read even more Cusk but don’t tell anyone. Anybody got any good reading recommendations? Let me know in the comments. ba dum tsssssss 🥁.

Frerk, is a 40-year-old independent research artist living with his vacuum robot in a small studio (but pretty central). He is a-okay, don’t worry about this unhinged post, I’m just kiddin’, I’m just jetlagged.
